newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Virgin eyes Chinese airline stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: Virgin eyes Chinese airline stake - paper.

text.p: Virgin Group is seeking to buy a stake in Chinese carriers China Eastern or Shanghai Airlines as part of a bid to become the first operator on the London-Shanghai route, the South China Morning Post said on Friday.

The newspaper quoted senior Virgin sources as saying the airline was interested in taking a stake in one of the two carriers to prove its commitment to the region -- before any decision on the first carrier to operate the London route.

Virgin chairman Richard Branson would only confirm that the airline had been involved in talks with Chinese mainland carriers, but declined to name the other parties to the discussions, it said. Officials from Virgin were not immediately available for comment.
Shanghai is not a designated location in the bilateral treaty between Britain and China, but Virgin and British Airways are lobbying hard to win the landing rights there.
British Airways is the only British carrier operating on the London-Beijing route and Branson has stressed that he is also keen for a share.
China Eastern plans to raise US$400 million late this year or early next year through the float of its shares on the Hong Kong and New York stock markets.
Shanghai Airlines, which has about a dozen aircraft operating domestic routes, was set up in 1985, and is 75 percent owned by the Shanghai government.
